content.text: I’ll inspect the discussion and the current mise checkout, then work out the concrete change it’s asking for. I’ll also do a quick history check because this touches the repository’s existing hk workflow and conventions.

The history check is using the repository’s Entire Search skill, which searches prior agent checkpoints rather than only Git commits. In parallel with the current-tree inspection, I’m treating the GitHub discussion text as the source of truth for scope.

The failure is reproducible from code inspection: the registry switched `hk@1.58.1+` to the Packslip backend, but that backend never implemented lock metadata resolution. Installation can fill the current platform after downloading, while `mise lock` falls back to an empty platform record—so `--locked` later has no URL. I’m narrowing the fix to Packslip’s lock resolver and a regression test for the hk boundary.

The implementation now verifies the Packslip manifest during lock generation, selects the artifact for each requested target platform, and records its signed SHA-256, URL, and signer. The first full format/build pass is still running; after that I’ll exercise the exact Windows-target lock case that previously produced an empty entry.

The code compiles under the repository’s full all-features check. The focused e2e is rebuilding the executable from scratch, so validation is taking longer than the code change itself; no test failure has appeared yet.

The new resolver passed its three key assertions—Windows platform entry, signed checksum/URL, and signer identity. The test’s later legacy-version assertion failed only because my inserted `mise lock hk@1.58.1` intentionally pruned the older configured version; I’m moving the new regression block after the existing boundary checks so it doesn’t disturb their fixture state.

Two review findings are valid and security-relevant: lock generation must reject a trusted stamp that lacks a manifest digest, and it must apply the same authenticated release-age cutoff as installation. I’m fixing both. I’m also strengthening the regression to exercise the locked-install boundary, but I’ll keep the cross-platform assertion because that is the original bug.

content.text: The stronger install test exposed an expected Packslip policy boundary: `--locked` still verifies the vendor’s current signed release policy, so it is not an offline-install mode. I’m keeping the locked-install assertion but removing `MISE_OFFLINE`; that will exercise the URL/checksum gate without asserting unsupported offline policy behavior.
